Sprint 4 migration for InkOS at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS` — Dodo Payments billing layer. Migrations exist through `20260415000006_storage_rls_hardening.sql`. `subscriptions` table already bootstrapped in migration #1 (service-role-only writes via webhook).

**New migration `supabase/migrations/20260415000007_billing_deposits.sql`:**

1. **Extend existing `subscriptions` table (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS):**
   - `dodo_customer_id text` — Dodo customer ID
   - `plan_tier text CHECK (plan_tier IN ('solo','studio','pro','enterprise'))` 
   - `billing_cycle text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monthly' CHECK (billing_cycle IN ('monthly','annual'))`
   - `trial_start timestamptz`
   - `trial_end timestamptz`
   - `current_period_start timestamptz`
   - `current_period_end timestamptz`
   - `cancel_at_period_end boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`
   - `cancelled_at timestamptz`
   - `price_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD'`
   - `quantity int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` — for per-seat tiers
   - `metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`
   - Index on `(studio_id, status)`, `(dodo_subscription_id)` unique
   - `status` CHECK in place from bootstrap — keep existing

2. **`plans`** — declarative plan catalog (not per-studio; seeded globally)
   - `tier text NOT NULL CHECK (tier IN ('solo','studio','pro','enterprise'))`
   - `billing_cycle text NOT NULL CHECK (billing_cycle IN ('monthly','annual'))`
   - `dodo_product_id text NOT NULL` — from env var mapping
   - `display_name text NOT NULL`
   - `price_cents int NOT NULL`
   - `currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD'`
   - `max_artists int` — null = unlimited
   - `max_locations int`
   - `sms_monthly_quota int`
   - `ai_generations_quota int` — null on non-Pro+
   - `features jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` — array of feature keys
   - `sort_order int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`
   - UNIQUE (tier, billing_cycle)
   - RLS: public SELECT allowed (anon + authenticated) — this is a public pricing catalog
   - No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies (service-role only — seeded via migration)
   - Seed 8 rows: solo/studio/pro/enterprise × monthly/annual with price_cents matching plan ($29/$59/$99/$199 monthly; $23/$47/$79/$159 annual × 100). `dodo_product_id` left as placeholder string `'DODO_PRODUCT_SOLO_MONTHLY'` etc. — env-driven mapping resolved at runtime

3. **`invoices`** — synced from Dodo webhooks
   - `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `subscription_id uuid REFERENCES subscriptions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
   - `dodo_invoice_id text NOT NULL`
   - `dodo_payment_id text`
   - `amount_cents int NOT NULL`
   - `tax_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `currency text NOT NULL`
   - `status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft','open','paid','uncollectible','void','refunded'))`
   - `period_start timestamptz`
   - `period_end timestamptz`
   - `due_date timestamptz`
   - `paid_at timestamptz`
   - `pdf_url text`
   - `hosted_url text`
   - `line_items jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`
   - `metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`
   - UNIQUE `dodo_invoice_id`
   - Index on `(studio_id, created_at DESC)`
   - RLS: studio SELECT own only; service-role INSERT/UPDATE (webhook writes)

4. **`payments`** — all payment transactions (subscription + deposit + balance)
   - `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `booking_id uuid REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` — null for subscription charges
   - `invoice_id uuid REFERENCES invoices(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
   - `client_id uuid REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` — for client-paying-deposit
   - `dodo_payment_id text NOT NULL`
   - `dodo_checkout_id text`
   - `type text NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('subscription','deposit','balance','tip','refund','adjustment'))`
   - `amount_cents int NOT NULL`
   - `currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD'`
   - `status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending','processing','succeeded','failed','refunded','partially_refunded'))`
   - `refund_amount_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `refund_reason text`
   - `description text`
   - `receipt_url text`
   - `failure_code text`
   - `failure_message text`
   - `succeeded_at timestamptz`
   - `refunded_at timestamptz`
   - `metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`
   - UNIQUE `dodo_payment_id`
   - Indexes: `studio_id`, `booking_id`, `client_id`, `(studio_id, succeeded_at DESC)`, `dodo_checkout_id`
   - RLS: studio SELECT own only; service-role INSERT/UPDATE

5. **`usage_meters`** — per-studio, per-period usage counters (for feature gates)
   - `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `period_start timestamptz NOT NULL`
   - `period_end timestamptz NOT NULL`
   - `meter text NOT NULL CHECK (meter IN ('sms_sent','ai_generations','bookings_created','active_artists','active_locations','storage_mb'))`
   - `used int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - `quota int` — resolved from plan at period start; null = unlimited
   - `overage_cents int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`
   - UNIQUE (studio_id, period_start, meter)
   - Index on `(studio_id, meter, period_end DESC)`
   - RLS: studio SELECT own only; authenticated INSERT/UPDATE via RPCs (service-role also)

6. **`feature_flags`** — per-studio overrides (Enterprise custom features, beta access)
   - `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `flag_key text NOT NULL`
   - `enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`
   - `expires_at timestamptz`
   - `reason text` — audit note
   - UNIQUE (studio_id, flag_key)
   - RLS: studio SELECT own; service-role write only (platform admin controls via admin panel)

7. **Update `bookings` table** — payment-related columns. Most already exist (deposit_cents, deposit_paid, deposit_paid_at, deposit_payment_id, tip_cents). Add:
   - `balance_payment_id text` — Dodo payment ID for post-session balance charge
   - `balance_paid boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`
   - `balance_paid_at timestamptz`
   - `total_paid_cents int GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((CASE WHEN deposit_paid THEN deposit_cents ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN balance_paid THEN (price_cents - deposit_cents) ELSE 0 END) + tip_cents) STORED`

8. **`refund_requests`** — cancellation deposit refunds workflow
   - `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `booking_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bookings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
   - `payment_id uuid REFERENCES payments(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
   - `requested_by uuid REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`
   - `amount_cents int NOT NULL`
   - `reason text`
   - `status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','approved','rejected','processed','failed'))`
   - `processed_at timestamptz`
   - `dodo_refund_id text`
   - `approver_notes text`

9. **RPCs:**
   - `public.get_studio_subscription(p_studio_id uuid) RETURNS jsonb` — authenticated only, returns subscription + plan + current usage meters. SECURITY DEFINER STABLE. Verifies studio membership.
   - `public.increment_usage_meter(p_studio_id uuid, p_meter text, p_amount int DEFAULT 1) RETURNS jsonb` — SECURITY DEFINER, atomically increments current period's meter, creates row if missing (current period = calendar month start/end of UTC now), returns new used count and whether quota exceeded. Used by API routes to enforce quotas.
   - `public.check_feature_access(p_studio_id uuid, p_feature_key text) RETURNS boolean` — resolves: if studio has active `feature_flags` override (and not expired) return that; else check plan tier's `features` jsonb array. Used by `lib/billing/feature-gate.ts`.
   - `public.get_billing_summary(p_studio_id uuid) RETURNS jsonb` — studio portal summary: current plan, next renewal, last 3 invoices, upcoming charges, trial status.

10. **Triggers:**
    - On `bookings` INSERT: call `increment_usage_meter(studio_id, 'bookings_created')` — non-blocking, log failure but don't abort
    - On `artists` INSERT with `status='active'` OR UPDATE to active: recalculate `active_artists` usage (just set to count, not increment — use `SELECT count(*)`)
    - On `locations` INSERT: same for `active_locations`

11. **RLS policies — every new table:**
    - `plans` — public SELECT (anon + auth), no writes
    - `invoices`, `payments` — studio SELECT own via `studio_id = ANY(public.user_studio_ids())`; no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from any role (service-role uses its own bypass)
    - `usage_meters` — studio SELECT own; authenticated INSERT/UPDATE (the RPC is SECURITY DEFINER so it bypasses; direct writes also allowed for future self-reporting)
    - `feature_flags` — studio SELECT own only; no writes
    - `refund_requests` — studio SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE own (owner/admin role-gated for UPDATE)

**Dodo webhook event types to document in handoff (Koda implements the webhook):**
- `subscription.created` / `subscription.updated` / `subscription.cancelled` / `subscription.trial_ended`
- `invoice.created` / `invoice.paid` / `invoice.payment_failed`
- `payment.succeeded` / `payment.failed` / `payment.refunded`
- `customer.updated`

**Seed statements:** Include 8 `INSERT INTO plans` at end of migration — 4 tiers × 2 cycles. Use the pricing grid from the plan (`/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/plans/immutable-conjuring-pelican.md` — Pricing & Feature Gating Matrix).

**Deliverables:**
1. Migration file (target: 600-900 lines)
2. Update `lib/supabase/types.ts` with new tables + columns
3. Write `.handoffs/sprint-4-dato-migration.md`: table inventory, RPC contracts, seed summary, webhook event map, Koda gotchas (idempotency via `webhook_events`, `dodo_payment_id` UNIQUE, GENERATED `total_paid_cents` never in INSERT/UPDATE, plan lookup by env var → plan_id)
4. Report: line count, table count, RPC count, trigger count, seed row count

**Rules:**
- CHECK constraints, never ENUM
- Idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`
- RLS enabled on every new table + at least one policy
- `dodo_payment_id`, `dodo_invoice_id`, `dodo_subscription_id` all UNIQUE indexes
- Service-role writes for webhook-owned tables
- All money in cents, all timestamps timestamptz
- Every FK has an index

1	# Code Change Discipline — Anti-Cascade Protocol
2	
3	> **Every agent that edits code files MUST follow this protocol.**
4	> This prevents the #1 problem: fixing one thing and breaking three others.
5	> Loaded by: Koda, Vex, Sage (enforcement), Luna (regression detection), Riko.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## THE PROBLEM THIS SOLVES
10	
11	When an agent edits a file without checking what depends on it, the fix cascades:
12	1. Agent changes function signature in `lib/auth.ts`
13	2. 12 files import from `lib/auth.ts` — all now have type errors
14	3. Agent "fixes" 3 of them, introduces a logic bug in the 4th
15	4. User has to re-prompt 3 more times to clean up the mess
16	
17	**This protocol ensures agents understand the blast radius BEFORE editing.**
18	
19	---
20	
21	## PRE-CHANGE: Impact Analysis (30 seconds, saves 30 minutes)
22	
23	Before editing ANY file, run this mental checklist:
24	
25	### 1. Who imports this file?
26	```bash
27	# Find all consumers of the file you're about to edit
28	grep -rn "from.*$(basename FILE .tsx)" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" app/ lib/ components/ workers/
29	```
30	Write down the count. If >5 files import it, this is a high-blast-radius change.
31	
32	### 2. What does this file export?
33	```bash
34	grep -n "export" path/to/file.ts
35	```
36	If you're changing an export signature (rename, add param, change return type), every consumer breaks.
37	
38	### 3. Is this a layout or provider?
39	Layouts cascade to ALL child routes. Providers cascade to ALL children.
40	```bash
41	# Check if this file is used as a layout
42	grep -rn "layout" app/ --include="layout.tsx" -l
43	```
44	**Layout changes = P0 blast radius. Test every child route after changing a layout.**
45	
46	### 4. Is this a shared component?
47	```bash
48	# How many files use this component?
49	grep -rn "ComponentName" --include="*.tsx" app/ components/ | wc -l
50	```
51	If used in >3 places → make your change, then verify ALL usage sites.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## DURING CHANGE: The 1-3-Verify Rule
56	
57	**Never edit more than 3 files before running verification.**
58	
59	```
60	CYCLE:
61	  Edit file 1 (maybe 2-3 if tightly coupled)
62	  → pnpm tsc --noEmit
63	  → pnpm build (if structural change)
64	  IF PASS → next cycle
65	  IF FAIL → fix THIS before touching anything else
66	```
67	
68	### Why 3 files max?
69	
70	- 1-3 files: Easy to understand what changed. Easy to revert.
71	- 4-7 files: Hard to track. Some changes mask others.
72	- 8+ files: You're doing a refactor, not a fix. Stop and plan.
73	
74	---
75	
76	## CHANGE CATEGORIES & RULES
77	
78	### Category A: Safe changes (low blast radius)
79	- Adding a new file that nothing imports yet
80	- Adding a new export to a file (existing exports unchanged)
81	- Editing JSX content (text, styling) without changing props
82	- Adding a new API route
83	
84	**Rule:** Normal 1-3-Verify cycle.
85	
86	### Category B: Risky changes (medium blast radius)
87	- Changing a function signature (params, return type)
88	- Renaming an export
89	- Moving a file to a different path
90	- Changing a shared component's props
91	
92	**Rule:** List ALL consumers first. Update every consumer in the same cycle. Verify.
93	
94	### Category C: Dangerous changes (high blast radius)
95	- Editing a layout file
96	- Editing a provider/context
97	- Changing the Supabase client setup
98	- Changing auth flow
99	- Editing middleware
100	- Changing `next.config.ts`
101	- Changing `package.json` dependencies
102	
103	**Rule:** Full test suite after change. Check every route that could be affected. If >10 routes affected, test at least 3 representative ones.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## POST-CHANGE: Regression Check
108	
109	After completing a fix, before reporting success:
110	
111	```bash
112	# 1. TypeScript (catches broken imports, wrong types)
113	pnpm tsc --noEmit
114	
115	# 2. Lint (catches formatting, unused imports)
116	pnpm lint
117	
118	# 3. Build (catches SSR issues, dynamic imports, missing env)
119	pnpm build
120	
121	# 4. Tests
122	pnpm test --run
123	
124	# 5. Quick smoke test (Stack A)
125	# Start dev server if needed, then:
126	curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/health | head -1
127	# Should return {"status":"ok"...}
128	```
129	
130	**ALL FIVE must pass. If any fail, you're not done.**
131	
132	---
133	
134	## COMMON CASCADES AND HOW TO PREVENT THEM
135	
136	### Cascade: Changing types.ts (Supabase generated types)
137	**Problem:** Regenerating types changes every table type. Components expecting old shape break.
138	**Prevention:** After `supabase gen types`, run `pnpm tsc --noEmit` immediately. Fix all errors in one batch.
139	
140	### Cascade: Changing a shared hook
141	**Problem:** `useAuth()` or `useUser()` used in 20+ components. Changing return shape breaks all.
142	**Prevention:** Don't change the return shape. Add new fields instead. Deprecate old ones gradually.
143	
144	### Cascade: Adding 'use client' to a file that was a Server Component
145	**Problem:** All child components now lose access to server-side data fetching.
146	**Prevention:** Extract the client-only part into a separate `ClientComponent.tsx`. Keep the parent as Server Component.
147	
148	### Cascade: Changing environment variable names
149	**Problem:** `.env.local`, `.env.example`, `railway.toml`, CI/CD, Supabase Edge Functions — all need updating.
150	**Prevention:** grep for the old var name everywhere:
151	```bash
152	grep -rn "OLD_VAR_NAME" . --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.toml" --include="*.yml" --include="*.env*"
153	```
154	
155	### Cascade: Updating a dependency version
156	**Problem:** Breaking changes in the dependency cascade through the codebase.
157	**Prevention:** Read the changelog/migration guide BEFORE updating. Update one dep at a time. Build after each.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## THE "I FIXED IT" CHECKLIST
162	
163	Before telling the user a fix is complete:
164	
165	- [ ] `pnpm tsc --noEmit` passes (zero errors)
166	- [ ] `pnpm lint` passes (zero errors, zero warnings on changed files)
167	- [ ] `pnpm build` succeeds
168	- [ ] `pnpm test --run` passes (if tests exist)
169	- [ ] I checked that files importing my changed file still work
170	- [ ] I did NOT add `any`, `@ts-ignore`, or `@ts-expect-error`
171	- [ ] I did NOT add `console.log` (use logger instead)
172	- [ ] I did NOT change more than what was needed for this fix
173	- [ ] The original problem is actually solved (I verified behavior, not just "no errors")
174	
175	**If you can't check ALL boxes, you're not done.**
176	
177	---
178	
179	## FOR VEX SPECIFICALLY: The Bug Fix Sequence
180	
181	```
182	1. REPRODUCE: Can I see the bug? (error message, screenshot, behavior)
183	2. LOCATE: Which file is the root cause? (not the symptom file)
184	3. ANALYZE: What imports this file? What will break if I change it?
185	4. FIX: Minimal change to root cause file (1-3 files max)
186	5. VERIFY: Does the bug go away? (check the actual behavior)
187	6. REGRESSION: Did I break anything else? (pnpm tsc + pnpm build + pnpm test)
188	7. DONE: All checks pass + bug is gone + nothing new is broken
189	```
190	
191	**Vex's biggest failure mode: fixing the symptom instead of the cause, then chasing cascading breakage. Step 2 (LOCATE root cause) is where Vex must spend the most time.**
192	
193	---
194	
195	## FOR KODA SPECIFICALLY: The Feature Build Sequence
196	
197	```
198	1. PLAN: What files am I creating/editing? What exists already?
199	2. TYPES: Define TypeScript types/interfaces first
200	3. DATA: Database migration + RLS + type generation
201	4. API: Server Actions or API routes (with Zod validation)
202	5. UI: Components (Server Components first, Client only when needed)
203	6. WIRE: Connect UI to data (React Query or direct fetch)
204	7. STATES: Loading, empty, error states for every data-dependent component
205	8. VERIFY: Full fix-verify loop (tsc, lint, build, test)
206	```
207	
208	**Koda's biggest failure mode: building UI before data layer is solid, then fighting type errors when wiring things up. Steps 2-4 MUST be verified before starting step 5.**

2	
3	> **Loaded by:** Dato (primary), Koda (when building data features), Arya (schema design), Sage (DB audit), Vex (DB debugging)
4	> **Stack:** Supabase Postgres (managed), `@supabase/ssr` for Next.js, `@supabase/supabase-js` for client

8	
9	## 1. MIGRATION SAFETY
10	
11	### Naming Convention
12	```
13	supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql
14	```
15	Example: `20260413120000_add_projects_table.sql`
16	
17	### Zero-Downtime Migration Rules
18	
19	**SAFE (no lock, no downtime):**
20	```sql
21	-- Add nullable column
22	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN description text;
23	
24	-- Add column with default (Postgres 11+ is instant)
25	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active';
26	
27	-- Create index concurrently (doesn't lock table)
28	CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_projects_user_id ON projects(user_id);
29	
30	-- Create new table
31	CREATE TABLE project_tags (...);
32	
33	-- Add foreign key (NOT VALID skips validation of existing rows)
34	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT fk_user
35	  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) NOT VALID;
36	-- Then validate separately (lighter lock):
37	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT fk_user;
38	```
39	
40	**DANGEROUS (locks table, causes downtime):**
41	```sql
42	-- ❌ Adding NOT NULL to existing column without default
43	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN description SET NOT NULL;
44	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Add check constraint
45	ALTER TABLE projects ADD CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null
46	  CHECK (description IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;
47	ALTER TABLE projects VALIDATE CONSTRAINT projects_description_not_null;
48	
49	-- ❌ Renaming a column (breaks all queries referencing old name)
50	ALTER TABLE projects RENAME COLUMN name TO title;
51	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: Expand-migrate-contract pattern
52	-- 1. Add new column: ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN title text;
53	-- 2. Backfill: UPDATE projects SET title = name WHERE title IS NULL;
54	-- 3. Switch app code to read/write title
55	-- 4. Drop old: ALTER TABLE projects DROP COLUMN name;
56	
57	-- ❌ Changing column type
58	ALTER TABLE projects ALTER COLUMN price TYPE numeric;
59	-- ✅ SAFE alternative: New column + backfill + swap
60	
61	-- ❌ CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY
62	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user ON projects(user_id);
63	-- ✅ Always: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
64	```
65	
66	### Migration Rollback Strategy
67	
68	Every migration file should have a corresponding rollback comment:
69	```sql
70	-- Migration: 20260413120000_add_projects_table.sql
71	-- Rollback: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS projects CASCADE;
72	
73	CREATE TABLE projects (
74	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
75	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
76	  name text NOT NULL,
77	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
78	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
79	);
80	```
81	
82	If a migration fails mid-flight:
83	1. Check what was applied: `SELECT * FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 5;`
84	2. Manually fix the state or apply the rollback SQL
85	3. Never delete a migration file that's been applied — create a new migration to undo it
86

89	## 2. RLS (Row Level Security) — COMPLETE PATTERNS
90	
91	### Pattern A: User-owned data
92	```sql
93	ALTER TABLE projects ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
94	
95	-- Users see only their own projects
96	CREATE POLICY "users_select_own" ON projects
97	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
98	
99	CREATE POLICY "users_insert_own" ON projects
100	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
101	
102	CREATE POLICY "users_update_own" ON projects
103	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id)
104	  WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
105	
106	CREATE POLICY "users_delete_own" ON projects
107	  FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
108	```
109	
110	### Pattern B: Team/org-scoped data
111	```sql
112	-- Members of an org can see org data
113	CREATE POLICY "org_members_select" ON projects
114	  FOR SELECT USING (
115	    org_id IN (
116	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
117	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
118	    )
119	  );
120	
121	-- Only admins can delete
122	CREATE POLICY "org_admins_delete" ON projects
123	  FOR DELETE USING (
124	    org_id IN (
125	      SELECT org_id FROM org_members
126	      WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND role = 'admin'
127	    )
128	  );
129	```
130	
131	### Pattern C: Public read, authenticated write
132	```sql
133	CREATE POLICY "anyone_select" ON blog_posts
134	  FOR SELECT USING (published = true);
135	
136	CREATE POLICY "authors_insert" ON blog_posts
137	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = author_id);
138	
139	CREATE POLICY "authors_update" ON blog_posts
140	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = author_id);
141	```
142	
143	### Pattern D: Service role bypass (for webhooks, background jobs)
144	```sql
145	-- Service role bypasses RLS by default in Supabase
146	-- But if you WANT policies for service role:
147	CREATE POLICY "service_role_all" ON projects
148	  FOR ALL USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
149	```
150	**In code:** Use `createClient(url, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)` for webhook handlers and background jobs. NEVER expose service role key to the browser.
151	
152	### RLS Performance Rules
153	```sql
154	-- ❌ SLOW: Subquery in every row check
155	CREATE POLICY "slow_policy" ON data
156	  FOR SELECT USING (
157	    user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM permissions WHERE ...)
158	  );
159	
160	-- ✅ FAST: Use a security definer function + cache
161	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.user_org_ids()
162	RETURNS uuid[] AS $$
163	  SELECT COALESCE(
164	    array_agg(org_id),
165	    '{}'::uuid[]
166	  )
167	  FROM org_members
168	  WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
169	$$ LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER STABLE;
170	
171	CREATE POLICY "fast_org_policy" ON data
172	  FOR SELECT USING (org_id = ANY(auth.user_org_ids()));
173	
174	-- Index to support the function
175	CREATE INDEX idx_org_members_user_id ON org_members(user_id);
176	```
177	
178	### RLS Testing
179	```sql
180	-- Test as a specific user
181	SET request.jwt.claims = '{"sub": "user-uuid-here", "role": "authenticated"}';
182	SET role = 'authenticated';
183	
184	-- Should return only user's rows
185	SELECT * FROM projects;
186	
187	-- Reset
188	RESET role;
189	RESET request.jwt.claims;
190	```
191	
192	### RLS Audit Query (Sage runs this)
193	```sql
194	-- Find tables WITHOUT RLS
195	SELECT schemaname, tablename
196	FROM pg_tables
197	WHERE schemaname = 'public'
198	AND tablename NOT IN (
199	  SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables
200	  WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND rowsecurity = true
201	);
202	-- Result must be EMPTY or deployment is blocked
203	```

207	## 3. DATABASE TRIGGERS & FUNCTIONS
208	
209	### Pattern: Auto-update `updated_at`
210	```sql
211	-- Reusable trigger function (create ONCE)
212	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_updated_at()
213	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
214	BEGIN
215	  NEW.updated_at = now();
216	  RETURN NEW;
217	END;
218	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
219	
220	-- Apply to any table
221	CREATE TRIGGER set_updated_at
222	  BEFORE UPDATE ON projects
223	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_updated_at();
224	```
225	
226	### Pattern: Auto-create profile on signup
227	```sql
228	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user()
229	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
230	BEGIN
231	  INSERT INTO public.profiles (id, email, created_at)
232	  VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.email, now());
233	  RETURN NEW;
234	END;
235	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;
236	
237	CREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created
238	  AFTER INSERT ON auth.users
239	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user();
240	```
241	
242	### Pattern: Audit trail trigger
243	```sql
244	-- Audit log table
245	CREATE TABLE audit_log (
246	  id bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
247	  table_name text NOT NULL,
248	  record_id uuid NOT NULL,
249	  action text NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')),
250	  old_data jsonb,
251	  new_data jsonb,
252	  user_id uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id),
253	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
254	);
255	
256	-- Enable RLS (only service role reads audit logs)
257	ALTER TABLE audit_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
258	CREATE POLICY "service_only" ON audit_log
259	  FOR ALL USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
260	
261	-- Generic audit trigger function
262	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.audit_trigger()
263	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
264	BEGIN
265	  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
266	    INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, record_id, action, old_data, user_id)
267	    VALUES (TG_TABLE_NAME, OLD.id, 'DELETE', to_jsonb(OLD), auth.uid());
268	    RETURN OLD;
269	  ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
270	    INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, record_id, action, old_data, new_data, user_id)
271	    VALUES (TG_TABLE_NAME, NEW.id, 'UPDATE', to_jsonb(OLD), to_jsonb(NEW), auth.uid());
272	    RETURN NEW;
273	  ELSIF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
274	    INSERT INTO audit_log (table_name, record_id, action, new_data, user_id)
275	    VALUES (TG_TABLE_NAME, NEW.id, 'INSERT', to_jsonb(NEW), auth.uid());
276	    RETURN NEW;
277	  END IF;
278	END;
279	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;
280	
281	-- Apply to any table that needs audit logging
282	CREATE TRIGGER audit_projects
283	  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON projects
284	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.audit_trigger();
285	```
286	
287	### Pattern: Soft delete
288	```sql
289	-- Add soft delete columns
290	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN deleted_at timestamptz;
291	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN deleted_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id);
292	
293	-- RLS policy excludes soft-deleted rows
294	CREATE POLICY "users_select_active" ON projects
295	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id AND deleted_at IS NULL);
296	
297	-- Soft delete function
298	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.soft_delete()
299	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
300	BEGIN
301	  NEW.deleted_at = now();
302	  NEW.deleted_by = auth.uid();
303	  RETURN NEW;
304	END;
305	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
306	
307	-- Instead of DELETE, UPDATE with trigger
308	-- App code: supabase.from('projects').update({ deleted_at: new Date().toISOString() }).eq('id', id)
309	```

313	## 4. INDEX STRATEGY
314	
315	### When to Create Indexes
316	```sql
317	-- Rule: Index every column used in WHERE, JOIN, ORDER BY, or RLS policy
318	
319	-- Foreign keys (ALWAYS index these — Postgres doesn't auto-index FKs)
320	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user_id ON projects(user_id);
321	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_org_id ON projects(org_id);
322	
323	-- Commonly filtered columns
324	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_status ON projects(status);
325	
326	-- Composite index for multi-column filters
327	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_user_status ON projects(user_id, status);
328	
329	-- Partial index (only index rows that matter)
330	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_active ON projects(user_id)
331	  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'active';
332	
333	-- GIN index for JSONB
334	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_metadata ON projects USING GIN (metadata);
335	
336	-- GIN index for full-text search
337	ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN fts tsvector
338	  GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', coalesce(name, '') || ' ' || coalesce(description, ''))) STORED;
339	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_fts ON projects USING GIN (fts);
340	
341	-- Trigram index for LIKE/ILIKE searches
342	CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
343	CREATE INDEX idx_projects_name_trgm ON projects USING GIN (name gin_trgm_ops);
344	```
345	
346	### EXPLAIN ANALYZE — How to Read Query Plans
347	```sql
348	EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT TEXT)
349	SELECT * FROM projects WHERE user_id = 'xxx' AND status = 'active';
350	
351	-- GOOD: "Index Scan using idx_projects_user_status"
352	-- BAD: "Seq Scan on projects" → Missing index
353	-- BAD: "Bitmap Heap Scan" on large table → Index exists but too many rows match
354	-- BAD: "Sort" with high cost → Add index for ORDER BY column
355	```
356	
357	### Index Maintenance
358	```sql
359	-- Check index usage (unused indexes waste write performance)
360	SELECT
361	  schemaname, tablename, indexname,
362	  idx_scan, idx_tup_read, idx_tup_fetch,
363	  pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) AS size
364	FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
365	WHERE idx_scan = 0  -- Unused indexes
366	ORDER BY pg_relation_size(indexrelid) DESC;
367	
368	-- Check table bloat
369	SELECT
370	  schemaname, tablename,
371	  pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(schemaname || '.' || tablename)) AS total_size,
372	  n_dead_tup, n_live_tup,
373	  ROUND(n_dead_tup::numeric / GREATEST(n_live_tup, 1) * 100, 1) AS dead_pct
374	FROM pg_stat_user_tables
375	WHERE n_dead_tup > 1000
376	ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC;
377	```

381	## 5. SUPABASE REALTIME SUBSCRIPTIONS
382	
383	### Pattern: Subscribe to table changes (React)
384	```tsx
385	'use client'
386	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
387	import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/client'
388	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
389	
390	type Project = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Row']
391	
392	export function useRealtimeProjects(userId: string) {
393	  const [projects, setProjects] = useState<Project[]>([])
394	  const supabase = createClient()
395	
396	  useEffect(() => {
397	    // Initial fetch
398	    supabase
399	      .from('projects')
400	      .select('*')
401	      .eq('user_id', userId)
402	      .then(({ data }) => {
403	        if (data) setProjects(data)
404	      })
405	
406	    // Subscribe to changes
407	    const channel = supabase
408	      .channel('projects-changes')
409	      .on(
410	        'postgres_changes',
411	        {
412	          event: '*',
413	          schema: 'public',
414	          table: 'projects',
415	          filter: `user_id=eq.${userId}`,
416	        },
417	        (payload) => {
418	          if (payload.eventType === 'INSERT') {
419	            setProjects(prev => [...prev, payload.new as Project])
420	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'UPDATE') {
421	            setProjects(prev =>
422	              prev.map(p => p.id === (payload.new as Project).id ? payload.new as Project : p)
423	            )
424	          } else if (payload.eventType === 'DELETE') {
425	            setProjects(prev =>
426	              prev.filter(p => p.id !== (payload.old as Project).id)
427	            )
428	          }
429	        }
430	      )
431	      .subscribe()
432	
433	    // CRITICAL: Cleanup on unmount
434	    return () => {
435	      supabase.removeChannel(channel)
436	    }
437	  }, [userId])
438	
439	  return projects
440	}
441	```
442	
443	### Realtime Rules
444	1. **Always clean up subscriptions** on component unmount (`removeChannel`)
445	2. **Use filters** (`filter: 'user_id=eq.xxx'`) to reduce payload — never subscribe to entire table
446	3. **RLS applies to Realtime** — users only receive changes they're authorized to see
447	4. **Enable Realtime per table** in Supabase Dashboard → Database → Replication
448	5. **Max channels:** ~100 per client connection. Pool carefully.
449	6. **Don't use Realtime for large datasets** — it sends full row payloads. For high-volume, use polling + React Query.
450	
451	### Enable Realtime on a table
452	```sql
453	-- In migration file
454	ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE projects;
455	```

457	---

459	## 6. SUPABASE EDGE FUNCTIONS
460	
461	### When to Use Edge Functions vs API Routes
462	- **Edge Functions:** Low-latency global execution, Deno runtime, ~50ms cold start. Use for: lightweight webhooks, image transforms, geolocation-based logic.
463	- **Next.js API Routes (on Railway):** Full Node.js, access to BullMQ/Redis, no cold start. Use for: complex business logic, background jobs, AI inference, heavy computation.
464	
465	**Default to API Routes.** Edge Functions only when latency from a specific region matters.
466	
467	### Edge Function Structure
468	```
469	supabase/functions/
470	  my-function/
471	    index.ts        # Entry point
472	    _shared/        # Shared code between functions
473	      cors.ts
474	      supabase.ts
475	```
476	
477	### Edge Function Template
478	```ts
479	// supabase/functions/my-function/index.ts
480	import { createClient } from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2'
481	
482	const corsHeaders = {
483	  'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
484	  'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type',
485	}
486	
487	Deno.serve(async (req: Request) => {
488	  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
489	    return new Response('ok', { headers: corsHeaders })
490	  }
491	
492	  try {
493	    const supabase = createClient(
494	      Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!,
495	      Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!
496	    )
497	
498	    const { data, error } = await supabase
499	      .from('projects')
500	      .select('*')
501	      .limit(10)
502	
503	    if (error) throw error
504	
505	    return new Response(JSON.stringify(data), {
506	      headers: { ...corsHeaders, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
507	    })
508	  } catch (err) {
509	    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: err.message }), {
510	      status: 500,
511	      headers: { ...corsHeaders, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
512	    })
513	  }
514	})
515	```
516	
517	### Deploy Edge Functions
518	```bash
519	supabase functions deploy my-function --project-ref $PROJECT_REF
520	```
521	
522	---
523	
524	## 7. SCHEMA DESIGN PATTERNS
525	
526	### Standard Table Template
527	```sql
528	CREATE TABLE public.{table_name} (
529	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
530	  -- ownership
531	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
532	  -- OR for org-scoped:
533	  -- org_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES orgs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
534	
535	  -- data columns here
536	
537	  -- timestamps (EVERY table gets these)
538	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
539	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
540	);
541	
542	-- RLS (EVERY table)
543	ALTER TABLE public.{table_name} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
544	
545	-- Policies (minimum: SELECT + INSERT for owner)
546	CREATE POLICY "{table}_select" ON public.{table_name}
547	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
548	CREATE POLICY "{table}_insert" ON public.{table_name}
549	  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);
550	CREATE POLICY "{table}_update" ON public.{table_name}
551	  FOR UPDATE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
552	CREATE POLICY "{table}_delete" ON public.{table_name}
553	  FOR DELETE USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
554	
555	-- Index foreign keys
556	CREATE INDEX idx_{table}_user_id ON public.{table_name}(user_id);
557	
558	-- Auto-update timestamp trigger
559	CREATE TRIGGER set_{table}_updated_at
560	  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.{table_name}
561	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_updated_at();
562	```
563	
564	### Enum Pattern (use CHECK constraint, not Postgres ENUM)
565	```sql
566	-- ❌ AVOID: Postgres ENUM (can't remove values, migration nightmare)
567	CREATE TYPE project_status AS ENUM ('active', 'archived');
568	
569	-- ✅ USE: CHECK constraint (easy to modify)
570	CREATE TABLE projects (
571	  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
572	    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'archived', 'deleted'))
573	);
574	```
575	
576	### JSONB for Flexible Data
577	```sql
578	-- Use JSONB for user preferences, metadata, settings
579	ALTER TABLE profiles ADD COLUMN preferences jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb;
580	
581	-- Query JSONB
582	SELECT * FROM profiles WHERE preferences->>'theme' = 'dark';
583	SELECT * FROM profiles WHERE preferences @> '{"notifications": true}';
584	
585	-- Index JSONB (GIN for containment queries)
586	CREATE INDEX idx_profiles_preferences ON profiles USING GIN (preferences);
587	```
588	
589	### Subscription/Billing Tables
590	```sql
591	CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
592	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
593	  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
594	  plan text NOT NULL CHECK (plan IN ('free', 'pro', 'team')),
595	  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
596	    CHECK (status IN ('active', 'past_due', 'canceled', 'trialing')),
597	  external_id text, -- Dodo payment ID or Shopify subscription ID
598	  current_period_start timestamptz,
599	  current_period_end timestamptz,
600	  cancel_at_period_end boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
601	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
602	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
603	);
604	
605	ALTER TABLE subscriptions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
606	CREATE POLICY "users_select_own_sub" ON subscriptions
607	  FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
608	-- Only service role can INSERT/UPDATE (from webhook handler)
609	CREATE POLICY "service_manage_subs" ON subscriptions
610	  FOR ALL USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
611	```
612	
613	---
614	
615	## 8. BACKUP & DISASTER RECOVERY
616	
617	### Supabase Managed Backups
618	- **Pro plan:** Daily backups, 7-day retention
619	- **Team plan:** Daily backups, 14-day retention
620	- **Enterprise:** Point-in-time recovery (PITR), 30-day retention
621	
622	### Manual Backup (before risky migrations)
623	```bash
624	# Dump full database
625	pg_dump $DATABASE_URL --format=custom --no-owner > backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).dump
626	
627	# Dump specific table
628	pg_dump $DATABASE_URL --format=custom --table=public.projects > projects_backup.dump
629	
630	# Restore from backup
631	pg_restore --dbname=$DATABASE_URL --no-owner --clean backup.dump
632	```
633	
634	### Pre-Migration Safety Script
635	```bash
636	#!/usr/bin/env bash
637	set -euo pipefail
638	# Run BEFORE any risky migration
639	
640	echo "Creating pre-migration backup..."
641	pg_dump "$DATABASE_URL" --format=custom --no-owner > "backup_pre_migration_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).dump"
642	echo "Backup complete: $(ls -lh backup_pre_migration_*.dump | tail -1)"
643	
644	echo "Checking current migration state..."
645	psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT version, name FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 5;"
646	
647	echo "Ready to apply migration. Backup is saved."
648	```
649	
650	---
651	
652	## 9. TYPE GENERATION WORKFLOW
653	
654	```bash
655	# From local Supabase (development)
656	pnpm supabase gen types typescript --local > lib/supabase/types.ts
657	
658	# From remote Supabase (staging/production)
659	pnpm supabase gen types typescript --project-ref $SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF > lib/supabase/types.ts
660	
661	# Verify types compile
662	pnpm tsc --noEmit
663	```
664	
665	### Using Generated Types
666	```ts
667	import type { Database } from '@/lib/supabase/types'
668	
669	// Table row type
670	type Project = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Row']
671	
672	// Insert type (omits auto-generated fields)
673	type ProjectInsert = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Insert']
674	
675	// Update type (all fields optional)
676	type ProjectUpdate = Database['public']['Tables']['projects']['Update']
677	
678	// Use in Supabase queries for type safety
679	const { data } = await supabase
680	  .from('projects')
681	  .select('id, name, status')
682	  .returns<Pick<Project, 'id' | 'name' | 'status'>[]>()
683	```
684	
685	**Rule: Regenerate types after EVERY schema change. If TypeScript complains about a column that exists in the database, the types file is stale.**
686	
687	---
688	
689	## 10. CONNECTION MANAGEMENT
690	
691	### Supabase Connection Pooling
692	Supabase uses PgBouncer (Supavisor) for connection pooling:
693	- **Port 5432:** Direct connection (limited connections, use for migrations only)
694	- **Port 6543:** Pooled connection (use for application queries)
695	
696	```
697	# .env
698	# For application (pooled)
699	DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres
700	
701	# For migrations (direct)
702	DIRECT_URL=postgresql://postgres.[ref]:[password]@aws-0-[region].pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres
703	```
704	
705	### Connection Limits
706	- **Free:** 60 direct + unlimited pooled
707	- **Pro:** 100 direct + unlimited pooled
708	- **Team:** 200 direct + unlimited pooled
709	
710	If hitting limits: reduce connection pool in application code, use pooled connection URL, close connections after use.
711	
712	---
713	
714	## 11. DEBUGGING DATABASE ISSUES
715	
716	### Empty Query Results (90% of the time: RLS)
717	```sql
718	-- Check if RLS is blocking
719	SET request.jwt.claims = '{"sub": "user-uuid"}';
720	SET role = 'authenticated';
721	SELECT * FROM projects; -- Does this return rows?
722	RESET role;
723	RESET request.jwt.claims;
724	```
725	
726	### Slow Queries
727	```sql
728	-- Find slow queries
729	SELECT query, calls, mean_exec_time, total_exec_time
730	FROM pg_stat_statements
731	ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC
732	LIMIT 10;
733	
734	-- Check missing indexes
735	SELECT
736	  relname AS table,
737	  seq_scan, seq_tup_read,
738	  idx_scan, idx_tup_fetch,
739	  CASE WHEN seq_scan > 0
740	    THEN ROUND(seq_tup_read::numeric / seq_scan, 0)
741	    ELSE 0
742	  END AS avg_rows_per_seq_scan
743	FROM pg_stat_user_tables
744	WHERE seq_scan > 100
745	ORDER BY seq_tup_read DESC;
746	-- High seq_tup_read + low idx_scan = missing index
747	```
748	
749	### Lock Contention
750	```sql
751	-- Check active locks
752	SELECT pid, mode, relation::regclass, granted
753	FROM pg_locks
754	WHERE NOT granted;
755	
756	-- Kill a blocking query (use with caution)
757	SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid);
758	-- Or force: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid);
759	```
760	
761	### Database Size Monitoring
762	```sql
763	-- Total database size
764	SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database()));
765	
766	-- Size per table
767	SELECT
768	  tablename,
769	  pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('public.' || tablename)) AS total,
770	  pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size('public.' || tablename)) AS data,
771	  pg_size_pretty(pg_indexes_size('public.' || tablename)) AS indexes
772	FROM pg_tables
773	WHERE schemaname = 'public'
774	ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size('public.' || tablename) DESC;
775	```
776	
777	---

60	## Data Model (Multi-Tenant, RLS-Enforced)
61	
62	`studio_id` is the tenant key on every domain table. RLS uses cached helper:
63	
64	```sql
65	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.user_studio_ids()
66	RETURNS uuid[] LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER STABLE AS $$
67	  SELECT array_agg(studio_id) FROM public.studio_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid();
68	$$;
69	-- Index: studio_members(user_id) — required for performance
70	```

-- =============================================================
-- SECTION 9 — RPC: increment_usage_meter
-- =============================================================
-- SECURITY DEFINER: bypasses RLS. Called by API routes to atomically
-- increment usage. Returns jsonb: { used, quota, exceeded }.
-- Period = calendar month (UTC). Creates row if missing.
-- =============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.increment_usage_meter(
  p_studio_id uuid,
  p_meter     text,
  p_amount    int DEFAULT 1
)
RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_period_start  timestamptz;
  v_period_end    timestamptz;
  v_used          int;
  v_quota         int;
  v_plan_tier     text;
  v_plan_row      public.plans%ROWTYPE;
BEGIN
  -- Compute current calendar month window (UTC)
  v_period_start := date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC');
  v_period_end   := v_period_start + interval '1 month';

  -- Resolve quota from the studio's current plan
  SELECT s.plan_tier INTO v_plan_tier
  FROM public.subscriptions s
  WHERE s.studio_id = p_studio_id
  LIMIT 1;

  -- Default to 'solo' if no subscription row yet
  v_plan_tier := COALESCE(v_plan_tier, 'solo');

  SELECT * INTO v_plan_row
  FROM public.plans
  WHERE tier = v_plan_tier
    AND billing_cycle = 'monthly'   -- quota is per-period regardless of billing cycle
  LIMIT 1;

  -- Derive quota from plan columns
  v_quota := CASE p_meter
    WHEN 'sms_sent'          THEN v_plan_row.sms_monthly_quota
    WHEN 'ai_generations'    THEN v_plan_row.ai_generations_quota
    WHEN 'bookings_created'  THEN NULL  -- unlimited bookings at all tiers
    WHEN 'active_artists'    THEN v_plan_row.max_artists
    WHEN 'active_locations'  THEN v_plan_row.max_locations
    WHEN 'storage_mb'        THEN NULL  -- unlimited storage (monitored, not enforced yet)
    ELSE NULL
  END;

  -- Upsert: increment if row exists, insert if not
  INSERT INTO public.usage_meters
    (studio_id, period_start, period_end, meter, used, quota)
  VALUES
    (p_studio_id, v_period_start, v_period_end, p_meter, p_amount, v_quota)
  ON CONFLICT (studio_id, period_start, meter) DO UPDATE
    SET used       = usage_meters.used + p_amount,
        quota      = v_quota,           -- refresh quota snapshot on every write
        updated_at = now()
  RETURNING used INTO v_used;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'used',     v_used,
    'quota',    v_quota,
    'exceeded', CASE WHEN v_quota IS NOT NULL AND v_used > v_quota THEN true ELSE false END
  );
END;
$$;

-- =============================================================
-- SECTION 10 — RPC: check_feature_access
-- =============================================================
-- Resolves: active feature_flags override takes precedence;
-- otherwise falls through to plan-level features jsonb array.
-- Used by lib/billing/feature-gate.ts.
-- =============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.check_feature_access(
  p_studio_id   uuid,
  p_feature_key text
)
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
STABLE
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_flag_enabled  boolean;
  v_flag_exists   boolean;
  v_plan_tier     text;
  v_features      jsonb;
BEGIN
  -- 1. Check explicit feature_flag override (not expired)
  SELECT enabled, true
  INTO v_flag_enabled, v_flag_exists
  FROM public.feature_flags
  WHERE studio_id = p_studio_id
    AND flag_key  = p_feature_key
    AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now())
  LIMIT 1;

  IF v_flag_exists THEN
    RETURN v_flag_enabled;
  END IF;

  -- 2. Fall back to plan features array
  SELECT s.plan_tier INTO v_plan_tier
  FROM public.subscriptions s
  WHERE s.studio_id = p_studio_id
  LIMIT 1;

  v_plan_tier := COALESCE(v_plan_tier, 'solo');

  SELECT pl.features INTO v_features
  FROM public.plans pl
  WHERE pl.tier          = v_plan_tier
    AND pl.billing_cycle = 'monthly'   -- features are identical across cycles
    AND pl.is_active     = true
  LIMIT 1;

  RETURN COALESCE(v_features ? p_feature_key, false);
END;
$$;

-- =============================================================
-- SECTION 11 — RPC: get_studio_subscription
-- =============================================================
-- Returns subscription + plan + current usage meters for the studio.
-- Caller must be a member of p_studio_id.
-- =============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.get_studio_subscription(
  p_studio_id uuid
)
RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
STABLE
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_sub       public.subscriptions%ROWTYPE;
  v_plan      public.plans%ROWTYPE;
  v_meters    jsonb;
  v_period_start timestamptz;
  v_period_end   timestamptz;
BEGIN
  -- Verify caller is a member of this studio
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.studio_members
    WHERE studio_id = p_studio_id AND user_id = auth.uid()
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'access_denied' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;

  -- Fetch subscription
  SELECT * INTO v_sub
  FROM public.subscriptions
  WHERE studio_id = p_studio_id
  LIMIT 1;

  -- Fetch matching plan (prefer same billing_cycle; fallback monthly)
  SELECT * INTO v_plan
  FROM public.plans
  WHERE tier          = COALESCE(v_sub.plan_tier, 'solo')
    AND billing_cycle = COALESCE(v_sub.billing_cycle, 'monthly')
    AND is_active     = true
  LIMIT 1;

  -- Current period usage meters
  v_period_start := date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC');
  v_period_end   := v_period_start + interval '1 month';

  SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(meter, jsonb_build_object(
    'used',   used,
    'quota',  quota
  )), '{}')
  INTO v_meters
  FROM public.usage_meters
  WHERE studio_id   = p_studio_id
    AND period_start = v_period_start;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'subscription', to_jsonb(v_sub),
    'plan',         to_jsonb(v_plan),
    'usage',        v_meters
  );
END;
$$;

| `price_cents` | `int` | `0` | Snapshot of price at time of subscription |

## New `bookings` Columns

## RPC Contracts

### `public.get_studio_subscription(p_studio_id uuid) → jsonb`
- Auth: authenticated, caller must be a studio member
- Returns: `{ subscription: {...}, plan: {...}, usage: { meter_name: { used, quota } } }`
- Use in: `/settings/billing` page, middleware plan checks

### `public.increment_usage_meter(p_studio_id uuid, p_meter text, p_amount int DEFAULT 1) → jsonb`
- Auth: SECURITY DEFINER (no RLS check inside function)
- Returns: `{ used: int, quota: int | null, exceeded: boolean }`
- Use in: every API route that consumes a metered resource (SMS send, AI generation, booking create)
- Idempotent: upserts by `(studio_id, period_start, meter)` — safe to call concurrently
- Period: always calendar month UTC — no parameter needed

### `public.check_feature_access(p_studio_id uuid, p_feature_key text) → boolean`
- Auth: SECURITY DEFINER STABLE
- Logic: feature_flags override first (respects `expires_at`) → plan.features jsonb array
- Use in: `lib/billing/feature-gate.ts` → call this RPC server-side, return 403 if false
- Feature keys match the `features` jsonb arrays in the `plans` rows

### `public.get_billing_summary(p_studio_id uuid) → jsonb`
- Auth: authenticated, caller must be a studio member
- Returns: `{ plan, status, billing_cycle, current_period_end, cancel_at_period_end, trial_end, in_trial, last_invoices[3], current_usage }`
- Use in: `/settings/billing` portal page — single RPC call, no N+1 queries

DO NOT hard-code actual Dodo product IDs in the database; the mapping belongs in code so it can differ between dev/staging/prod.

## Webhook Event Map (Koda implements `app/api/webhooks/dodo/route.ts`)

All events arrive at the existing webhook endpoint. Idempotency is already handled via `webhook_events` table — check `(source, event_id)` UNIQUE before processing any event.

| Event | Action |
|-------|--------|
| `subscription.created` | INSERT into `subscriptions` (or UPSERT by `studio_id`) — set `plan_tier`, `billing_cycle`, `trial_start`, `trial_end`, `status = 'trialing'`, `dodo_subscription_id`, `dodo_customer_id`, `current_period_start`, `current_period_end`, `price_cents` |
| `subscription.updated` | UPDATE `subscriptions` by `dodo_subscription_id` — update status, period dates, `cancel_at_period_end`, `price_cents` |
| `subscription.cancelled` | UPDATE `subscriptions` — set `status = 'canceled'`, `cancelled_at = now()` |
| `subscription.trial_ended` | UPDATE `subscriptions` — set `status = 'active'` (or `'past_due'` if payment failed) |
| `invoice.created` | INSERT into `invoices` — set `status = 'open'`, period dates, line_items |
| `invoice.paid` | UPDATE `invoices` — set `status = 'paid'`, `paid_at` |
| `invoice.payment_failed` | UPDATE `invoices` — set `status = 'open'` (or `'uncollectible'`); UPDATE `subscriptions.status = 'past_due'` |
| `payment.succeeded` | UPSERT into `payments` by `dodo_payment_id` — set `status = 'succeeded'`, `succeeded_at`; UPDATE `bookings.deposit_paid = true` or `balance_paid = true` by `dodo_payment_id` match |
| `payment.failed` | UPSERT into `payments` — set `status = 'failed'`, `failure_code`, `failure_message` |
| `payment.refunded` | UPDATE `payments` — set `status = 'refunded'`, `refund_amount_cents`, `refunded_at`; UPDATE `refund_requests.status = 'processed'` if matching |
| `customer.updated` | UPDATE `subscriptions.dodo_customer_id` by studio lookup |

## Koda Gotchas

### 1. Idempotency is mandatory
Every webhook handler must check `webhook_events` first:
```ts
const { data: existing } = await supabase
  .from('webhook_events')
  .select('id')
  .eq('source', 'dodo')
  .eq('event_id', event.id)
  .single()

if (existing) return NextResponse.json({ ok: true }) // already processed
```

### 2. `dodo_payment_id` UNIQUE constraint
`payments.dodo_payment_id` has a UNIQUE constraint. Use UPSERT (`ON CONFLICT (dodo_payment_id) DO UPDATE`) not plain INSERT in the webhook handler to handle Dodo's at-least-once delivery.

### 3. `total_paid_cents` is GENERATED — never write it
The column is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS ... STORED`. Supabase will throw `ERROR: column "total_paid_cents" can only be updated to DEFAULT` if you include it in an INSERT or UPDATE. The TypeScript types already exclude it from `Insert` and `Update` — if you see a type error mentioning this column, you've added it somewhere you shouldn't have.

### 4. Plan lookup: env var → product ID → plan row
`plans.dodo_product_id` contains placeholder strings like `'DODO_PRODUCT_PRO_MONTHLY'`. The real Dodo product IDs live in env vars. Resolution pattern:
```ts
// lib/dodo/products.ts
const PRODUCT_MAP: Record<string, { tier: PlanTier; billingCycle: BillingCycle }> = {
  [process.env.DODO_PRODUCT_SOLO_MONTHLY!]:     { tier: 'solo',       billingCycle: 'monthly' },
  [process.env.DODO_PRODUCT_SOLO_ANNUAL!]:      { tier: 'solo',       billingCycle: 'annual' },
  [process.env.DODO_PRODUCT_STUDIO_MONTHLY!]:   { tier: 'studio',     billingCycle: 'monthly' },
  // ... etc
}
```
On `subscription.created`, look up `product_id` from the Dodo payload → resolve tier/cycle from this map → write to `subscriptions.plan_tier` and `subscriptions.billing_cycle`.

### 5. Service-role for all webhook writes
All webhook writes to `invoices`, `payments`, `subscriptions` MUST use the service-role client (already established in `app/api/webhooks/dodo/route.ts`). Authenticated client will be silently rejected because there are no INSERT/UPDATE policies for those tables.

### 6. `refund_requests` workflow
- Client/reception creates request via app → INSERT with `status = 'pending'`
- Owner/admin reviews → UPDATE to `'approved'` or `'rejected'`
- Webhook handler processes Dodo refund → UPDATE to `'processed'` (service-role)
- Never process a refund in the same request cycle as creating it — always two steps

### 7. `check_feature_access` is server-side only
Call this RPC from Server Components or API route handlers. NEVER call it in Client Components — it reveals plan capabilities that should be enforced server-side only. The client can receive a 403 response; it should not pre-check.

### 8. Feature gate implementation pattern
```ts
// lib/billing/feature-gate.ts
export async function requireFeature(
  supabase: SupabaseClient,
  studioId: string,
  featureKey: string
): Promise<void> {
  const { data: hasAccess, error } = await supabase
    .rpc('check_feature_access', { p_studio_id: studioId, p_feature_key: featureKey })

  if (error || !hasAccess) {
    throw new FeatureGateError(featureKey)  // caught by API route → returns 403
  }
}
```
